capabilities.target: executive's calendar (accept invites) and triggers the document-search/email prep workflow
executive's documents, including board materials and draft financial results
any recipient, sent from the executive's mailbox

inputs.source: Calendar invites sent by anyone, including outside the company; the description is free text authored by the sender

instructions.note: The agent is instructed to accept invites, search the drive, and email attendees with no restriction on which documents are relevant, who the attendees are, or whether the invite sender's identity is verified.

The only stated oversight is a daily summary the agent writes about its own actions; no structural control is described, so safety depends entirely on the agent behaving as instructed even when acting on attacker-supplied invite text.

elements.name: Executive's document store (board materials, draft financial results)
Daily summary reviewed by the executive

controls.name: Daily summary reviewed by executive
controls.decay_rationale: The summary is authored by the same agent that may be acting on injected invite instructions; a more capable or hijacked model can omit or reframe the problematic send in its own summary (ASI09), so this control does not reliably catch the issue even today, and weakens further under model_upgrade.

controls.name: Human approval gate on mail.send, raw action review
controls.decay_rationale: A raw_action gate requiring a human to see the full recipient list and content before send is enforced outside the model and does not decay with model capability, though it can degrade under high approval volume (approval fatigue).

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to a verified directory, not the invite's attendee list
controls.decay_rationale: Destination addresses would be drawn from a vetted system of record rather than from attacker-controlled invite metadata or model choice, so it does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Separate least-privilege credential scoping between drive.search_and_read and mail.send
controls.decay_rationale: Scoped credentials enforced at the identity layer do not decay with model capability; the model cannot egress data it has no credential to send or access.

controls.name: Spotlighting/segregation of calendar invite free text as untrusted data
controls.decay_rationale: Even if added, this depends on the model respecting the delimiting of untrusted content, so it weakens under model_upgrade and is not sufficient alone.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): calendar invite injection drives restricted-document read and external mail send

attack_path.note: Untrusted, attacker-writable free-text invite description reaches the agent
Agent auto-accepts the invite and triggers the prep workflow described or implied by the invite content
Agent searches and reads board materials and draft financial results (restricted data)
Agent emails a brief containing document content to all invite attendees, including any external or attacker-controlled address, with no recipient restriction or approval

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Model or version string change in subject.model; rising volume of invites processed per day without added approval gates; or an increase in max_unattended_steps/removal of the daily review step.

evidence.observation: Prompt instructs the agent to accept invites automatically if the time is free, then search the drive and email a brief to attendees, with no identity or content verification.
Anyone can send the executive a calendar invite; the invite description is free text authored by the sender, which can inject instructions into the agent's prep step.
mail.send has no recipient restrictions and no approval step, and the executive's drive holds board materials and draft financial results (restricted data).
The daily summary is written by the agent itself, so oversight relies on a self-report rather than an independent record.

recommendations.action: Require a human approval gate with raw_action review before mail.send fires for any recipient not already a verified internal contact, especially when triggered by an invite-derived prep workflow.
Bind the outbound recipient list to a vetted directory/system of record rather than the invite's attendee list, so an attacker-added external address cannot receive the brief.

Scope drive.search_and_read and mail.send under separate least-privilege credentials, or add a check preventing restricted-sensitivity content read in one step from flowing into an external send in the same workflow without review.
Add an independent, tamper-evident audit log of agent actions, not authored by the agent, so oversight does not rely solely on the agent's self-written daily summary.
Treat calendar invite descriptions as untrusted data: quarantine or spotlight the free text so it is not interpreted as instructions during the prepare step.

rating.rationale: One present finding (the lethal trifecta: an untrusted calendar invite drives a read of restricted board/financial documents and an external email send) sets every tier. The source is untrusted (anyone can send an invite with attacker-controlled free text), the sink is S3 severe (irreversible egress of restricted data with no recipient restriction), and autonomy A3 has no step or runtime cap, so inherent is critical. The only declared control, a daily summary, is behavioral, dependent, and detective, earning no residual tier credit under the rubric, so residual equals the inherent floor at critical. Forecast stays critical because the tier is already at the ceiling; model upgrades and autonomy increases would further erode the self-written summary's already-limited detective value. Five structural and behavioral controls are recorded as missing_recommended because none of the preventive controls needed to lower this floor (approval gate, recipient confirmation, credential scoping, independent audit, input segregation) are present in the design.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.
No MCP/tool manifest or IaC was provided; exact credential scoping of drive.search_and_read and mail.send is inferred from the runtime notes at medium-to-high confidence.
No orchestration or approval configuration was provided beyond the system prompt; autonomy level A3 is taken as declared, with no step or runtime limits stated.
